name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.28.0 (2026-08-27) is a hardening release that caps cache replay at 10 MB per topic, limits message titles to 1 KB and tags to 512 bytes, and applies the visitor bandwidth budget to poll requests. Recent prior releases (v2.27.0, v2.26.x, v2.25.0) added email-based login, password reset via magic links, message template DoS protections, a fail2ban-compatible abuse ban-feed, and configurable date/time formats in the web app. PostgreSQL support was promoted from experimental to stable in v2.27.0. Full release notes are available at https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL-2.0 (client) — dual-licensed; check the repository for exact terms
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026 with frequent bug fixes, security hardening, and new features
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — username/password, access tokens, email-based login, and per-topic access control are supported

breaking_excerpts: Message title limited to 1 KB and all tags combined to 512 bytes; requests exceeding these limits are rejected with HTTP 400 (error codes 40057/40058) — previously no size limit existed.
Cache replay capped at 10 MB per topic per poll request; responses exceeding the cap are truncated and carry an X-Messages-Truncated: 1 header.
Message cache databases from ntfy older than v1.10.0 (November 2021) can no longer be migrated; upgrade via an older ntfy version first or delete the cache database.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a powerful multi-platform notification library supporting dozens of services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server like ntfy.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device notifications and file sharing with a polished UX but is a closed-source cloud service with limited free tier, unlike ntfy's fully open self-hosted approach.

alternatives.name: Ntfy.sh (self-hosted PushBot / Matrix/Synapse bots)
alternatives.review: Matrix/Synapse offers federated, encrypted messaging and notifications with self-hosting but is far more complex to operate than ntfy's simple HTTP pub-sub model.
